workbookName: Time Bandits Dev Set — Accepted (script tier, 10 rows)

rows.synopsis: A boy struggles to make the most of everyday life—until a bumbling gang of thieves lands in his bedroom.
rows.situation: having a passion your family laughs at; being told you are stuck in the past; being right and finally meeting people who value it
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: Madame Chung, 1810 Macau). Who learns: Kevin learns his history knowledge is worth something when Madame Chung acts on his advice (Bosun, change course), and the bandits begin to value the kid they planned to leave behind. Emotion: sad covers the family putdowns (stuck in the past, little worrier); proud lands when his strategy wins and Cassandra names his future. Coping: talking it out: the move is Kevin speaking up with what he knows and people acting on it; considered standing up for yourself but he never argues back, he offers. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly. Cassandra's you are important and will save the universe lands the worth theme. Synopsis em dash kept verbatim per the quoted-source exception.

rows.synopsis: On a whirlwind journey to ancient Mexico, Kevin and the Bandits take part in a feast. Pure Evil sends huntress Fianna on a quest.
rows.situation: being wrong in front of everyone; hearing that you always do the wrong thing; needing one friend to say it is not all your fault
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: Lady Sak K'uk'). Who learns: Kevin learns his mistake does not define him when Judy answers his parents-putdown confession (They say that to you? Out loud like that?) with it is not just your fault, and the bandits take him back. Emotion: sad carries the putdown echo (Maybe I'm the best at doing the wrong thing); embarrassed lands on What must everyone think of me. Coping: talking it out: the resolution is Judy's talk-it-through with Kevin; the episode also models apologizing when Kevin returns stolen goods (I took it from you when I didn't know you. I do apologize). Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly.

rows.synopsis: The Bandits pose as dragon slayers in England and feel the wrath of a wicked sheriff. Saffron embarks on her own search for answers.
rows.situation: a bully whose power only works because everyone goes along; being afraid to speak up to a tyrant; helping the people who carry out the orders see it
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: sheriff of Nottingham). Who learns: Kevin learns the sheriff's power collapses when the henchmen see it (If none of us are torturing, then no one's getting tortured), and the henchmen learn they can refuse and release the villagers. Emotion: scared is the village under threat and the bandits in the dungeon; brave lands when Kevin walks the henchmen through refusing. Coping: standing up for yourself: the story's turn is the collective refusal Kevin talks into being; considered reframing but the move is the refusal, not a recast. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly. Penelope's fake witch magic (the tiny prison box) stalls the sheriff; the dragon-slayer fame is comic set dressing.

rows.synopsis: Kevin and the Bandits run for their lives during New York's Harlem Renaissance. Saffron and an ally work to outwit enemies in Japan.
rows.situation: reading about life instead of living it; being nudged to try a new thing; saying an honest no when someone moves too fast
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: Madame Queenie). Who learns: Kevin learns you cannot keep reading about things happening (You have to make it happen. Live a little) when he walks into his first rent party, and Emmie learns an honest no works (this is really only our fourth conversation). Emotion: nervous/worried is Kevin at the threshold of a first-ever crime (even by his own library-copy standard); happy the jazz night. Coping: trying again: Kevin approaches the new experience instead of another book; considered talking it out but nothing is being resolved, the move is joining in. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly. Alto's courtship and the gangster mixup (Babyface, Madame Queenie mistaken identity) drive the comedy; guns stay cartoonish.

rows.synopsis: While searching for Kevin's home, the Bandits cross paths with Casanova and the Earl of Sandwich. Penelope is challenged to a duel.
rows.situation: missing a parent who is far away or in trouble; having hurt a friend by putting something else first; watching grown-ups settle a quarrel with a duel
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: Earl of Sandwich duel). Who learns: Penelope learns ambition ahead of a friend's life needs an apology (I may have valued my ambition ahead of my friend's life. And for that, I'm sorry), and Kevin learns his sadness can be noticed and helped (Judy: you seem a little sad lately). Emotion: sad is Kevin missing his coaled parents (My parents are dead); scared sits in the duel and the demon chase. Coping: apologizing: Penelope's out-loud apology and the forgiveness-and-compromise line are the story's turn; considered talking it out but the apology is the named move. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly.

rows.synopsis: The Bandits scour the desert for a missing member and hatch a plan to rob history's richest man. Widgit delves into the mysteries of the Map.
rows.situation: wanting to help a sad friend; working up the courage to tell someone how you feel; choosing between a comfortable new place and the people who need you
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: Mansa Musa). Who learns: Kevin learns a sad friend needs a purpose (he arranges the pretend theft with Mansa Musa, like you did with me), Bittelig learns to say the feeling out loud (You have to tell her how you feel), and Kevin chooses his quest over staying where he is appreciated. Emotion: sad is Penelope's lost purpose (She's sad and confused); brave is Kevin walking away from the welcome he always wanted. Coping: talking it out: the episode's fixes all happen through said-out-loud feelings, Bittelig's coaching and Kevin's ask to the mansa; considered naming the feeling but the coaching conversation is the modelled move. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly. Topics: none of the nine buckets fits a friendship-and-purpose story in a medieval caravan, left empty per the guide.

rows.synopsis: Saffron saves the day in an icy situation. Penelope faces off with a tribal chief. Bittelig puts his heart into a rescue mission.
rows.situation: missing a parent who is far away or gone; wanting to give up when a hard rescue keeps failing; caring for an injured animal that cannot ask for help
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: Twonicorn). Who learns: Kevin and Saffron learn to keep going when everything fails (I just gave up, answers Penelope, and we're not gonna give up), and the cavepeople learn an injured friend is worth saving (we are going to save it so it can have a future). Emotion: sad is the sibling miss-you talk (I miss them. Do you miss them?); brave is the walk of fear and the unicorn rescue. Coping: trying again: the mantra is explicit and repeated across every plotline (the leg, the acting, the escape); considered patience but the story celebrates pushing on, not waiting. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly. Topics: none of the nine buckets fits an Ice Age survival-and-unicorn story (cavemen are not Dinosaurs content), left empty per the guide.

rows.synopsis: Kevin and Saffron return to Bingley...but it's 1996 and their parents are children. Fianna continues her chase and crashes a goth party.
rows.situation: trying to stop something bad from happening and failing; being scared and told you are brave; saying sorry for the everyday wrongs
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: young Mum and Dad, 1994). Who learns: Kevin learns a failed rescue is not the end (It's okay, we'll try again. We'll come back another time), Saffron learns to say the sorry list out loud to her dad, and Bittelig learns doing one important thing (the medicine and the care book) counts. Emotion: scared is said outright (I'm really scared) and answered (you're incredibly brave); brave is the answer and the save. Coping: trying again: the phrase is the episode's hinge after the failed save; considered apologizing but the try-again is what carries Kevin's arc, while the sorries stay Saffron's subplot. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly. The Susan backstory (they tried many times and eventually gave up) keeps the honesty: some big things cannot be stopped.

rows.synopsis: The gang sets out to find the missing piece of the Map. Kevin comes face-to-face with the Supreme Being, who offers a tempting deal.
rows.situation: wondering what your point is when your plans keep failing; feeling replaced when old friends return; learning a team's job is looking out for each other
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: Susan, bubonic plague). Who learns: Penelope learns to say the doubt out loud (What's the point of us?) and hears the answer that sticks (We're a team. We look out for each other... even the newest members of our team), then acts on it by taking Kevin to the fortress. Emotion: hopeless is Penelope's we haven't done any of the things we set out to do; happy lands in the team answer and Susan's return. Coping: naming the feeling: Penelope names the pointlessness aloud and the bandits act on the naming with a new purpose, so the shown-mattering test passes; considered talking it out but the naming is the move. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly.

rows.synopsis: Despite impossible odds, Kevin, Saffron, and the Bandits venture into the Fortress of Darkness to save Kevin's parents.
rows.situation: facing a scary villain to get your family back; an idea the grown-ups call a failure turning out to be the one that works; wanting the family together again
rows.notes: Script-verified: Gestdown English subtitles (SuperSubtitles), downloaded 2026-11-16; content-checked against catalog synopsis (identity keyword: Fortress of Eternal Darkness). Who learns: Kevin and Saffron learn their own quick trick (the lunch box map swap) succeeds where the fail-proof plan Bittelig mocked collapses, and the family learns the point was being together (I just want us all being together). Emotion: scared is the Fortress of Darkness and Pure Evil himself; happy is the reunion and the send-off. Coping: trying again: the first plan fails and gets captured, and the kids adapt mid-failure; considered asking for help (Hen the giant carries them) but the resolution lands on the kids' own move, worth a vocabulary-review flag. Age 8-10 on TV-PG evidence (peril, demon threat, mild crude language); vibe silly. The Supreme Being's great reset plot closes the season arc; Hen of the giant head is comic support.
